contexts.text: Simulation and deceit were then abominable, and an enormous crime. AC 1118:end. AC 7361:end.
Under Hypocrite, see this reference. AC 8870:end. DMin 4653. CanonsNC 26. Redemption. 3. 7.
In the simulation itself... is the end...
The sphere of those who have indulged in simulatory practices is turned into the stench of vomit. SE 1045.
(It is in consequence of possessing an interior man that simulation is possible to man.)
Inwardly their voice is strident, because from the simulation of good.
The men of the Church (now) have deadly hatreds, invested with simulations of what is honourable.
The Most Ancients were entirely ignorant of what simulation is.
Simulations of what is honourable are taken away there.
Simulation which has good for the end. See Cunning.
Influx from the cerebellum into the face when there is not what is simulated.
Such speech (by the face) prevails with these Spirits (from another orb) because they cannot dissemble, that is, think one thing and show another in the face.
The face of those who from youth have been accustomed to simulation is contracted. Explained.
I could perceive from the mere tone... whether they spoke from what was simulated.
Man (too) can perceive whether there is what is simulated...
(The inhabitants of Mars) do not know what fraudulent simulation is. AC 7480.
The reason the faces (in Jupiter) are smiling... is that they never dissemble, that is, speak otherwise than they think.
For simulation, hypocrisy, cunning, and deceit, which now are called prudence, induce such effects (on the face).
Under Deceit, see this reference.
Dissemblingly, occurs. See Hypocrite.
To counterfeit and simulate these things is to make a likeness...
For by the external he simulates the things of Heaven.
The face of everyone (in the Sixth Earth) is an index... it simulates and counterfeits nothing.
In a face not taught to simulate all affections present themselves...
Hence a merely natural man can... simulate heavenly things by his acts.
The quality of this correspondence... with hypocrites, dissemblers...
The fourth kind of profanation is by those who... simulate affections...
As in the world they had simulated good affections... they are at first kept by turns in their externals...

Those who have simulated that they were in the good of love... hide themselves in caves; and those who have simulated that they were in truths of faith... hide themselves in the rocks of the mountains.
The exterior man has learned from childhood... to simulate...
The external will often partakes of simulation and dissimulation. This will the wife sees through, and does not conjoin herself with it except pretendedly or playfully.
Hence every man not interiorly led by the Lord is a pretender. (Continued. See Hypocrite.)

Are quite distinct from hypocritical simulations.
These conjugial simulations with a spiritual man and with natural men. Explained. CL 281.
The assumed favours... become more or less simulatory.
Either he must favour his wife dissemblingly, or...

In the other life men cannot simulate.
The simulation at once shines forth...
The Angels perceive the simulations of man. Explained.
Simulatory poetry.
(There are) those who want to dissemble with words and praises, and thus act solely as dissemblers... and those who desire to simulate for the sake of self-honour and gain.

(This) is a species of simulation.
On simulation, or those who speak otherwise than they think.
On a certain kind of persuasions and simulation.
He simulated piety, etc. DMin 4751.
